title: A repeated awakening study exploring the capacity of complexity measures to capture dreaming during propofol sedation
description: This dataset comprises repeated-awakening EEG recordings collected during propofol sedation, designed to explore dream experiences and consciousness dynamics under anesthesia. EEG data were acquired across wakefulness (eyes open/closed) and multiple sedation and awakening conditions, including sessions with transcranial magnetic stimulation. The study aims to evaluate whether EEG complexity measures can capture subjective dream reports elicited through repeated awakenings during propofol-induced sedation.
methods_description: EEG data were recorded using BrainVision hardware across conditions including wakefulness (eyes open/closed), sedation rest periods, and repeated awakenings during propofol sedation, with some sessions incorporating transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS). Data files include raw EEG signals, header and marker files, and event/channel metadata organized per subject following BIDS conventions.
